brand_focus: Cooking tips, recipes, and marinades with AI-styled ingredient photography. Audience is Europe-first, US a strong second. Goal: grow followers fast-but-safe by making every post highly shareable (sent to a friend) and saveable.

slots.note: Tue ~18h — w1-18 is the strongest confirmed slot (avg reach 1.8, 6 posts). Technique leads on reach (1.8, 4 posts) and hasn't been featured in this slot before; diversifies away from marinade overload while testing technique's ceiling.
Wed ~12h — w2-12 shows 2.0 reach on 1 post; small sample but highest reach observed. Lunchtime browse-and-save behaviour suits quick-dinner save-bait. Need more posts here to confirm.
Thu ~12h — w3-12 avg reach 1.7 on 3 posts, solid mid-week slot. Marinade is brand-core and still the most-posted theme; keeping one weekly slot to maintain signal without overcrowding.

Fri ~10h — w5-10 showed 2.0 reach (1 post, adjacent Saturday morning slot used as proxy). Friday morning browse before weekend cooking suits technique save-bait. Replaces weak w4-19 slot (reach dropped to 1.5 on 2 posts).

content_plan.technique: One foundational cooking technique relevant to home cooks — e.g. how to build a fond, reverse-sear, bloom spices, or emulsify a pan sauce. Slide 1: hero shot of the dramatic visual payoff of the technique (e.g. a perfectly seared crust, a glossy emulsified sauce) — pure food photography, zero text, numbers, labels, or graphics anywhere on the image. Slide 2: flat-lay or close-up of the key tools or ingredients that make the technique work — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3-4: two-beat before/after visual sequence showing the technique mid-action and the finished result — no text overlays of any kind. Final slide: close-up detail of the texture, colour, or finish that makes the result unmistakably worth the technique. ALL explanations, ratios, timing, troubleshooting tips, and step-by-step instructions belong in the caption exclusively.
content_plan.quick-dinner: A complete weeknight dinner built around one hero ingredient that comes together fast. Slide 1: hero shot of the finished dish plated beautifully — rich colour, clean surface, pure food photography with absolutely no text, numbers, or labels on the image. Slide 2: flat-lay of the raw ingredients loosely arranged by colour — purely photographic. Slides 3-4: a two-beat visual sequence showing one key technique moment (e.g. sear in pan, sauce going in) followed by the finished result — no text overlays of any kind. Final slide: close-up of texture and colour detail that makes the dish feel craveable and achievable. ALL ingredient quantities, timing, steps, swaps, and any written information belong in the caption only.
content_plan.marinade: One complete marinade built around a single protein or seasonal occasion. Slide 1: hero shot of the marinated, deeply coloured, glistening protein on a clean dark or neutral surface — pure food photography, zero text, numbers, or labels anywhere on the image. Slide 2: aesthetic flat-lay of raw marinade ingredients grouped loosely by colour and texture — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3-4: visual process contrast — protein submerging into the marinade, then the vivid colour and sheen transformation after marinating — no overlaid text or graphics of any kind. Final slide: finished plated dish in warm directional light, garnished but not cluttered. ALL ratios, quantities, timing, substitution tips, and step information belong in the caption exclusively.

caption_strategy: Every caption must open with a search-friendly hook sentence that names the dish or technique explicitly (e.g. 'This lemon-herb chicken marinade is the reason your weeknight dinners taste restaurant-quality') — Instagram indexes caption keywords for discovery. Follow with a save-prompt in the first three lines ('Save this before you forget it'). Then deliver genuine value: full ingredient quantities, ratios, timing, and step-by-step method in plain prose or a tight numbered list — all textual information that cannot appear on images must live here. Close with a conversational question to prompt comments ('What protein would you try this on?'). Keep total caption length 150–300 words; avoid emoji clutter but use 2–3 strategically to break up text.
hashtag_strategy: Use exactly 4–5 hashtags placed at the end of the caption after a line break. Prioritise one mid-size niche tag directly matching the theme (e.g. #marinaderecipe, #cookingtechnique, #quickdinner), one slightly broader food tag (#homecooking or #weeknightdinner), one evergreen search tag (#easyrecipes or #cookingathome), and optionally one seasonal or ingredient-specific tag for discoverability. Avoid mega tags above 50M posts — they bury young accounts instantly. Rotate and track which combinations correlate with reach improvements as data accumulates.
learnings: All engagement metrics (sends, saves, follows) remain at zero across 21 posts and all themes — the account has no meaningful signal yet beyond raw reach. Reach differences are small (1.0–2.0) and most slot data is thin (1–3 posts). Key actions: stop over-indexing on marinade (8 posts, no differentiation in engagement); rotate in technique which ties for highest reach (1.8) with more headroom. Retire sauce — lowest reach (1.5), 6 posts, zero engagement. Hold cadence at 4/week; do NOT increase until sends or saves register above zero. Prioritise search-keyword-rich captions and save-prompts as the primary lever since reach-to-follow conversion is also zero.
